working_claim: ChatGPT/GPT-3.5 generation reached Azure OpenAI preview on 9 March 2023.
reason: Blocked on a registry defect rather than on evidence. Both facts are true of different models.
target: Split the registry before recording this. Introduce gpt-3-5-turbo as a distinct model with ChatGPT as an alias, leave gpt-3-5 as the generation, then reassign the existing events and add this preview against the new id. That change also needs an OpenAI vendor baseline for gpt-3-5-turbo, since chatgpt-launch-2022-11-30 is scoped to the generation. Source already found: the Microsoft Azure blog of 9 March 2023, 'ChatGPT is now available in Azure OpenAI Service'.
resolution: The registry defect that blocked this is fixed. gpt-3-5-turbo now exists as a distinct model, so the March preview no longer contradicts the GPT-3.5 generation being generally available on Azure since January 2023. Neither existing gpt-3-5 event needed reassigning: the ChatGPT launch of November 2022 and the Azure service GA of January 2023 both legitimately mean the generation. A vendor baseline was added at the same time, openai-gpt3-5-turbo-2023-03-01, giving an eight-day lag to Azure. The item's own title conflated ChatGPT with the generation, which is what made it look unrecordable.
